label: Ушка / Юшка
description: A 10-sentence card for the folksy suffix -ушка/-юшка.

missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: бабушка from баба. The folksy suffix -ушка turns баба into бабушка 'grandmother', a warm, everyday term of affection.
Strategic focus: дедушка from дед. The suffix -ушка softens дед 'grandfather' into дедушка, adding folksy warmth and familiarity.
Strategic focus: избушка from изба. The suffix -ушка turns изба 'peasant hut' into избушка 'little hut', a small, folksy, fairy-tale dwelling.
Strategic focus: головушка from голова. The suffix -ушка makes голова 'head' into головушка, a folksy, lyrical, pitying form common in folk songs.
Strategic focus: соловушка from соловей. The suffix -ушка turns соловей 'nightingale' into соловушка 'dear nightingale', a tender, folk-poetic diminutive.
Strategic focus: краюшка from край. The suffix -юшка turns край 'edge, crust' into краюшка 'little crust', a homely, rustic word for a hunk of bread.
Strategic focus: contrast изба and избушка. The plain изба names a full hut, while избушка with -ушка signals a small, folksy one; the pair shows the suffix adding smallness.

missions.phrase: Бабушка и дедушка живут в деревне.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: бабушка and дедушка from баба and дед. The suffix -ушка gives both kin terms their warm, folksy, everyday flavour.
Strategic focus: головушка from голова. Here -ушка lends головушка a lyrical, folk-song colouring, expressing emotion more than literal size.
Strategic focus: соловушка from соловей. The suffix -ушка makes соловушка 'dear nightingale' a tender, folksy name for the singing bird.
